newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh tribal rebels abduct six Bengalis.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh tribal rebels abduct six Bengalis.

text.p: Separatist tribal rebels have kidnapped six Bengali-speaking people, including two government officials, in Bangladesh's southeastern Chittagong Hill Tracts, military sources said on Saturday.
They said the six travelling on a boat were attacked by Shanti Bahini (peace force) guerrillas at Thanchi in Bandarban hill district on Friday afternoon.
"The rebels took the victims, including local administrator Azimuddin Ahmed Chowdhury and civil engineer Mohammad Shahjahan, away from the boat," one official said.
"They have not come back nor there is any idea where they might be. It is now believed they have been adbucted," he told reporters.

Shanti Bahini abducted 28 Bengalis, mostly woodcutters, at gunpoint in nearby Rangamati district in September and shot them all dead. Some of the victims were beheaded, police and army officials said.

The Shantis. made up of mostly Chakma tribesmen, began an armed campaign in the 5,500 sq-mile (14,200 sq-km) Hill Tracts, bordering India and Burma, in 1973 after Bangladesh rejected their demand for autonomy.
They also want that some 300,000 Bengali-speaking settlers should be expelled from the hill and forest region.
Officials say over 8,500 people including rebels, soldiers and civilians have been killed in the insurgency, which has also forced thousands of tribal families to seek refuge in India.
The latest abductions followed a proposal by the Bangladesh government for peace talks with the rebels on Decmber 21, officials said on Saturday.
They said the Shantis had not yet responded to the offer.
The rebels earlier this month extended a truce with government forces until end of December.
